newsitem.title: USA: Weak dollar, profit-taking seen marring Dow at open.
newsitem.headline: Weak dollar, profit-taking seen marring Dow at open.

text.p: Strong profit-taking coupled with weakness on bonds and the dollar stood ready to erode U.S. stocks at the opening on Thursday, although some economic data due before the opening could ease selling.

"We still have an hour to go, so it could get better, but it looks like we'll see some profit-taking. It's high time we got some profit-taking for the short-term," said Hildegard Zagorski, analyst for Prudential Securities.
The Dow stormed up Wednesday 97 points to about 6178.

The dollar plummeted in Asia after an official from Japan's Ministry of Finance said Japan did not want the dollar to grow much stronger aganist the yen, raising fears that its strong-dollar policy was under threat. It stabilized at weak levels in European trading
Standard & Poor's December futures fell 3.4 to 726.10 and the 30-year U.S. Treasury bond fell 21/32 to yield 6.67 percent.

"We could see a fall of 30 to 40 points early in the session," said Peter Cardillo, director of research at Westfalia Investments. But he said after the pull-back, markets might be able to recover during the session.
"We've got some economic news coming and I suspect the 30-year Treasury auction will go well, and as a result the bond market could firm up later in the session," he said.
At 0830 EST/1330 GMT, weekly jobless claims are due. Economists are forecasting they will rise slightly to 344,000 compared to 342,000 in the earlier week.
At 1000 EDT/1500 GMT, third-quarter productivity and labor costs figures are due. The U.S. government will also launch the third part of its bond auction, selling 30-year issues, later today.

Tokyo stocks tumbled 220.41 points or 1.05 percent to finish at 20,771.11. London stocks were weak, but stable near session lows with the FTSE 100 off 29.1 to 3906.6. U.S. shares traded in London were sharply lower, pressured by the dollar.
Only Intel Corp bucked the trend, after the company forecasted strong fourth quarter earnings after the market close on Wednesday.
The New York Times Marketplace column spotlights the whether Bennett LeBow may be picking a fight with financier Carl Icahn at RJR Nabisco Holdings.
The Wall Street Journal's Heard on the Street column examines what the purchase of MCI Communications Corp could do for British Telecommunications's stock.
The Journal's "Intrinsic Value" columm reports that America Online may have done some balance sheet "spinning."
